name: Carpe Diem Gap Semester (Guatemala & Costa Rica and other routes)
summary: Ten-week small-group overseas semester with homestays, service placements and group travel, run for students aged 17-22. Routes include Central America, Southeast Asia, India & Nepal, Italy & Greece and Hawai'i.
other_eligibility: Health/medical form and interview; no academic prerequisites. Some routes require vaccinations and a physician sign-off.
cost_note: Tuition $16,900 for the 2026 70-day (10-week) Guatemala & Costa Rica semester. Tuition covers all food, accommodation, scheduled program activities and international travel insurance. EXCLUDES international airfare, which Carpe Diem itself estimates at $1,200-$1,500, plus personal spending money, passport and any visa fees. Realistic all-in cost is therefore about $18,100-$18,400, not $16,900. Deposit amount is not published on the program page; request it in writing before applying. Other routes are priced separately and the 8-week Italy & Greece and 5-week Guatemala summer options cost less.
financial_aid_note: Need-based scholarships and payment plans are offered; Carpe Diem does not publish typical award sizes, so ask for the median award before assuming aid will close the gap. 529 plans can be applied when college credit is taken.
college_credit_note: Optional college credit is offered through Carpe Diem's academic partner institution (historically Portland State University; confirm the current grantor directly). WARNING: earning college credit during a gap year can be costly. Credits earned after high school graduation can convert a deferred freshman admit into a TRANSFER applicant at some colleges, and transfer status usually forfeits incoming-freshman merit scholarships and first-year-only institutional aid. Ask your admitting college's registrar and financial aid office IN WRITING before electing credit.
funding_note: Independently operating and publishing programs through Fall 2027. No public distress signals found.

deadlines.note: Rolling admissions; programs fill and close by route. Fall semesters typically close in spring.

caveat_note: Pricing on the program page is honest about airfare being extra, which is better than many competitors. Marketing leans heavily on 'transformation' language; the underlying product is a supervised group tour with homestays and short volunteer placements, not a credentialed academic program. Carpe Diem does not disclose what share of the fee goes to marketing or overhead.

name: Latitudes Year
summary: Full-year program pairing one group semester overseas with a second semester in a self-directed volunteer placement in one of 20+ countries. Aimed at students who want a longer and more independent structure than a single gap semester.
other_eligibility: Health screen and interview. Second-semester independent placement requires demonstrated readiness; not all applicants are approved for it.
cost_note: 2025-2027 tuition $25,800 (Central America, Hawai'i, India & Nepal, Southeast Asia) to $29,800 (Italy & Greece). A single standalone semester of the independent placement is $9,900. Tuition includes orientation, the customized volunteer placement, a $3,100 placement stipend applied toward second-semester meals and accommodation, up to 12 college credits per semester, and international travel insurance. EXCLUDES international airfare, which Carpe Diem estimates at $3,400-$5,600 for the year, plus visa costs and spending money. Realistic all-in cost is roughly $29,200-$35,400. Deposit not published.
financial_aid_note: Need-based scholarships and payment plans; 529 College Savings Plans may be applied toward program costs when credit is taken. Typical award size not disclosed.
college_credit_note: 6-12 semester credits per semester are available, granted through Carpe Diem's partner institution (confirm the current grantor in writing). WARNING: accumulating up to 24 credits in a gap year is enough to trigger transfer-applicant status at many colleges. Transfer applicants generally lose incoming-freshman merit awards, first-year-only institutional grants and sometimes guaranteed housing. If you hold a deferred admission, get written confirmation from that college's registrar and financial aid office that the credits will not change your entering-student classification.
funding_note: Active and enrolling for 2026-2027.

deadlines.note: Rolling; the independent-placement semester requires lead time for matching, so early application is materially better.

caveat_note: The $3,100 'stipend' is not income to the participant; it is a budget allocated toward the student's own meals and lodging in semester two and is already inside the tuition figure. Do not read it as the program paying the student.

name: Pacific Discovery Gap Year Semester
summary: Small-group educational travel semesters in New Zealand, Australia, Southeast Asia, South America and elsewhere, blending adventure travel, conservation work and cultural immersion. Runs fall and spring cohorts.
other_eligibility: Health and fitness disclosure; some programs include diving or trekking components requiring medical clearance.
cost_note: Pacific Discovery publishes a rate of roughly $1,500-$2,000 PER WEEK; the $15,000-$20,000 range shown here is that weekly rate applied to a typical 10-week semester and is DERIVED, not a quoted per-program price. Confirm the exact figure for your specific route on their availability page, which was not machine-readable at time of research. Tuition covers accommodation, meals, activities, staffing and pre-departure support. EXCLUDES flights: Pacific Discovery tells students to budget an additional $800-$2,500 for return airfare depending on departure city. Also excludes visa fees and personal spending. Payment schedule: 50% of tuition due within 30 days of acceptance, balance due 20 June for fall programs and 15 November for spring programs.
financial_aid_note: Limited scholarships are advertised; amounts are not published. Treat this as close to full-pay.
college_credit_note: Credit is available on some itineraries through a partner university, but is not the default and is not the reason most students enroll. If you do elect credit, note that post-high-school credit can reclassify a deferred freshman admit as a transfer applicant, which typically voids incoming-freshman merit scholarships and first-year-only aid. Verify with your college in writing first.
funding_note: Actively publishing 2026, 2027 and 2028 departure dates. No distress signals found.

deadlines.note: Rolling by departure. Final payment 20 June (fall) / 15 November (spring).

caveat_note: Price is a derived estimate from the operator's own stated weekly range, not a quoted program price; verify before relying on it. The 50%-due-within-30-days payment term is aggressive and front-loads family cash exposure well before departure. Check the refund and cancellation schedule carefully.

name: Rustic Pathways Gap Semester
summary: Multi-week guided gap semesters in Fiji, Latin America and Thailand combining service projects, language immersion and adventure travel with a high staff-to-student ratio. Sits at the premium end of the guided-travel market.
other_eligibility: Health form; diving-based Fiji program requires medical clearance for scuba certification.
cost_note: Published 2026 gap semester tuition: Thailand 40 days $13,000; Spanish Immersion & Service (Costa Rica/Peru/Dominican Republic) 78 days $17,645; South Pacific Service & Ocean Skills (Fiji) 77 days $20,990. ALL are quoted 'plus airfare' - flights are NOT included. Rustic additionally charges a flight-handling fee: $450 plus airfare for chaperoned flights, $150 plus airfare for Rustic-arranged flights, or $0 if you book entirely on your own. So the Fiji program at $20,990 plus roughly $1,500-$2,000 in Pacific airfare plus a $450 chaperone fee is realistically $22,900-$23,400. Comprehensive insurance, all meals, housing and in-country transport ARE included. Deposit amount not published on the program page.
financial_aid_note: Rustic Pathways operates a foundation offering need-based scholarships, but award sizes for gap semesters are not published. Assume close to full pay unless you obtain a written offer.
college_credit_note: Rustic Pathways gap semesters are not primarily credit-bearing; any credit option is via a third-party partner and should be confirmed directly. If credit is elected, be aware that post-high-school credits can convert a deferred admit into a transfer applicant and thereby forfeit incoming-freshman merit and first-year-only institutional aid. Confirm with the college's registrar in writing.
funding_note: Large, long-established for-profit operator with a substantial school-travel business alongside gap programs. Actively publishing 2026 and 2027 pricing.

deadlines.note: Rolling enrollment by departure date.

caveat_note: At roughly $200-$270 per day this is one of the most expensive per-day options in the guided-travel category, and the participant performs volunteer labor rather than receiving wages. The flight-handling fee structure ($450 / $150 / $0) is a real line item families miss. Rustic is a for-profit company; no share-of-fee-to-marketing disclosure is published.

name: Winterline Global Skills Program
summary: DEFUNCT. Winterline ran a multi-country 'practical skills' gap year that taught 100+ hands-on skills across three continents. It no longer operates and its former domain has been sold to an unrelated business.
other_eligibility: N/A - program no longer operating.
cost_note: DO NOT PAY THIS OPERATOR. No current price exists because the program is not running. Historically the 9-month global skills program was priced in the high $30,000s excluding personal airfare to the start point, but that figure is obsolete and is provided only to help families recognize old marketing pages. Any site or broker currently quoting a Winterline price should be treated as suspect.
college_credit_note: Historically offered limited credit via a partner institution. Moot - program does not operate.
funding_note: CLOSED. As of August 2026 winterline.com no longer belongs to the education company: the domain resolves to a digital-asset and domain-brokerage firm advertising 'stealth acquisitions' and premium domain sales, meaning the education business sold or lost the domain. Third-party gap-year directories list Winterline programs as unavailable. Separately, prospective participants posted public complaints on the company's own social channels alleging that money was taken and the company went silent without issuing refunds. Treat any Winterline enrollment solicitation as high risk.
caveat_note: Students still find archived Winterline marketing pages and third-party directory listings that make the program look live. It is not. The most useful thing a directory can tell a family here is: this operator is gone, do not send a deposit. Confidence is medium rather than high only because no formal bankruptcy or dissolution filing was located; the domain transfer, absent programming and refund complaints are nonetheless consistent and decisive in practice.

name: Verto Education Semester Abroad
summary: First-year-of-college-abroad program in Buenos Aires, Prague, London, Florence and Seville, delivering accredited coursework alongside travel. Marketed as a credit-bearing alternative to a conventional freshman year rather than a classic gap year.
other_eligibility: High school diploma or equivalent; standard admissions review. Visa required for most destinations and is the student's responsibility.
cost_note: Fall 2026 semester tuition ranges $18,750-$33,500 depending on location. Included: course registration, housing, airport reception, orientation, digital books, excursions, staff support and travel medical insurance. EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED per Verto's own FAQ: airfare, travel and property insurance beyond the basic medical cover, visa costs, passport fees and personal expenses. Florence adds an optional meal plan at $1,500. Budget $800-$1,800 airfare plus $150-$500 visa depending on country, so a $18,750 headline is realistically $20,000-$21,000 and the top of the range approaches $36,000. A deposit is required to hold a place but the amount is not published; contact billing@vertoeducation.org. An early-deposit discount of $1,000 was offered for a January application deadline.
financial_aid_note: Verto offers a Scholars Award of $1,500-$5,000 based on GPA, a need-based Global Citizen Scholarship that Verto says can reduce out-of-pocket cost by as much as $17,000 (this typically means a homestay-based placement rather than a cash grant), an Opportunity Grant limited to Pell-eligible students who file FAFSA, and a $1,000 early-deposit discount. Scholars Award deadlines: 1 October for spring, 1 March for fall.
college_credit_note: CREDIT/AID INTERACTION - READ THIS FIRST. Courses and credits are delivered by Verto's accredited academic provider, the University of New Haven, and are designed to transfer. Verto's own FAQ states that VERTO IS NOT ELIGIBLE FOR FEDERAL FINANCIAL AID, which directly contradicts third-party write-ups and some marketing copy claiming FAFSA funds, Pell Grants and subsidized loans can be applied to Verto tuition. Get the current answer in writing from Verto before assuming federal aid applies. Separately, because Verto awards a full semester (or year) of real transferable credit, students who complete it frequently enter their destination college as TRANSFER students rather than first-year students. Transfer classification commonly forfeits incoming-freshman merit scholarships, first-year-only institutional grants, guaranteed housing and honors-college eligibility, and it can convert a deferred admission offer into a new transfer application with no guarantee of readmission. Verto's Direct Transfer Pathway with partner colleges is intended to mitigate this, and partner schools such as University of South Carolina, University of Colorado Boulder and University of Tennessee run branded Verto pathways with defined terms. If your college is NOT a Verto partner, obtain written confirmation from its registrar and financial aid office about entering classification and aid before enrolling. This is the single largest hidden cost in the program.
funding_note: Active and enrolling for Fall 2026 and 2027 with named university partnerships. A separate affiliated entity, The Verto Fund, exists for scholarship support.

deadlines.note: Early deposit deadline for the $1,000 tuition discount (now passed). General admission is rolling.
Verto Scholars Award application deadline for Spring 2027.
Verto Scholars Award application deadline for Fall 2027.

caveat_note: The federal-aid question is genuinely contradictory across sources: Verto's own FAQ says the program is not eligible for federal financial aid, while multiple third-party reviews and some Verto blog copy assert FAFSA and Pell funds can be used. Families should assume NOT eligible until Verto confirms otherwise in writing. The 'reduce your cost by up to $17,000' claim for the Global Citizen Scholarship describes a substituted housing model, not a $17,000 cash award. Because Verto is priced like a private college semester but does not carry that college's aid, the net price can exceed what the student would have paid at their admitting institution.

name: EF Gap Year
summary: Multi-destination gap year and gap semester programs combining language study, city immersion and group travel across Europe, Asia and Costa Rica. Unusually for this category, EF includes flights in the tuition.
other_eligibility: High school completion; visa requirements vary by itinerary and are the student's responsibility.
cost_note: $43,750 for the 23-week gap year program, 2026-2027. This is a confirmed price for the 23-week option only. INCLUDED, unusually: round-trip flights from your home city at the start of each semester, all inter-city transit by bus/plane/train, hotel and hostel accommodation in fall, apartment-style housing in spring, and roughly 50% of meals in fall plus one group dinner per week in spring. EXCLUDED: roughly half of all meals (budget $1,500-$3,000 for food over 23 weeks), visa fees, personal spending, and any independent travel. EF also markets 40-week 'World Year', 24-week 'Build Your Year' and 12-week semester options; PRICES FOR THOSE WERE NOT PUBLICLY CONFIRMED and EF does not publish them on the website - you must call for a quote. Deposit amount not published.
financial_aid_note: EF advertises scholarships and payment plans but does not publish award sizes or eligibility criteria online. Treat as full-pay unless you secure a written award.
college_credit_note: EF Gap Year is not a credit-bearing degree program; any academic credit is arranged through third-party partners and is not the core offering. If you do pursue credit, note that credits earned after high school graduation can reclassify a deferred admit as a transfer applicant, forfeiting incoming-freshman merit awards and first-year-only institutional aid. Confirm with your college's registrar in writing.
funding_note: EF Education First is a very large, financially stable privately held global education company. Counterparty risk is low relative to small independent gap operators.

deadlines.note: Rolling enrollment by departure; popular itineraries fill early.

caveat_note: $43,750 for 23 weeks is roughly $1,900 per week and is among the most expensive gap options indexed, though flights being included makes the comparison less unfavorable than the headline suggests. EF does not publish semester pricing online, which forces a sales conversation to learn the number - budget for that friction. Only about half of meals are covered in the fall term despite the premium price; this is a real and frequently underestimated add-on.

name: ARCC Gap Semester
summary: Ten-week small-group gap semesters in Southeast Asia, Latin America, Africa and the Western US, mixing service work, outdoor travel and cultural immersion. Long-running operator with a comparatively transparent financial aid policy.
other_eligibility: Health form and interview; physically active itineraries.
cost_note: $16,388 for the 70-day (10-week) Southeast Asia gap semester. Tuition covers accommodation, meals, activities and in-country ground transport. EXCLUDES international AND in-country flights - ARCC's own page flags that both are additional, which for a Southeast Asia itinerary with internal hops can add $1,500-$2,500, putting realistic all-in cost near $18,000-$19,000. Travel insurance coverage is not confirmed as included on this program page; verify. DEPOSIT: $1,000 due within one week of an admission offer, applied toward tuition. Payment schedule: 50% of remaining tuition due 1 June, 100% due 1 August for fall programs. Other ARCC destinations are priced separately.
financial_aid_note: Comparatively generous and unusually well-disclosed: need-based aid up to $6,000 with a stated typical award of $2,000-$4,000, plus additional scholarships that can add up to $10,000. The Voyagers Scholarship offers up to five awards per semester of $5,000-$8,000 to students identifying within the BIPOC community. Ask for the aid decision before paying the $1,000 deposit.
college_credit_note: ARCC maintains a dedicated college credit page and offers optional credit through a partner institution; confirm the current grantor and credit count directly. WARNING: credit earned after high school graduation can convert a deferred freshman admit into a transfer applicant at some colleges, which typically forfeits incoming-freshman merit scholarships and first-year-only institutional aid. Get written confirmation from your college's registrar and financial aid office before electing credit.
funding_note: Long-established operator, actively enrolling. No public distress signals found.

deadlines.note: Offers made before 1 June require a $1,000 deposit within one week; 50% of tuition due 1 June, balance 1 August.
Spring cycle deposit trigger date.

caveat_note: The 'in-country flights additional' clause is easy to miss and matters more here than for single-country programs - a Southeast Asia itinerary can involve several internal flights. ARCC publishes actual aid ranges, which is better disclosure than most competitors and worth crediting.

name: Take Action Lab (formerly Global Citizen Year Fellowship)
summary: RESTRUCTURED AND RENAMED. Global Citizen Year became Tilting Futures in 2024 and replaced its original 8-month country-immersion Fellowship with the shorter Take Action Lab, a semester-length apprenticeship program in Cape Town, South Africa or Penang, Malaysia. The organization is still operating and enrolling for 2027.
other_eligibility: Application, essays and interview. Visa required for South Africa or Malaysia placement.
cost_note: Take Action Lab (semester, ~12 weeks) $21,000. Take Action Lab Accelerator (9-week summer) $10,500. Tuition covers apprenticeship matching, shared housing, programming and a living-expense stipend that is spent by the student on their own costs (it is not income). Tilting Futures markets 'no hidden costs' but a separate Tuition Breakdown document governs; AIRFARE IS NOT CLEARLY INCLUDED IN BASE TUITION - financial aid is described as covering 'tuition and some travel expenses' and the Accelerator separately offers up to $2,300 toward flights for qualifying students, which strongly implies airfare is a student expense at list price. Budget $1,200-$2,000 for airfare to Cape Town or Penang plus visa fees unless you receive an explicit written flight allowance. Deposit amount not published.
financial_aid_note: Need-based financial aid and merit scholarships, historically substantial - this organization was built around access and has a long track record of large awards for lower-income students. Accelerator students may receive up to $2,300 specifically for flights. Apply for aid at the same time as admission; contact admissions@tiltingfutures.org.
college_credit_note: Both Take Action Lab and the Accelerator offer college credit granted by the UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH. WARNING: this is real transferable credit and therefore carries the standard gap-year risk - credits earned after high school graduation can cause a college to classify you as a transfer applicant rather than an entering first-year student, which commonly forfeits incoming-freshman merit scholarships, first-year-only institutional grants and honors eligibility, and can invalidate a deferred admission offer. Confirm the treatment in writing with your admitting college's registrar and financial aid office before electing credit.
funding_note: ACTIVE but MATERIALLY RESTRUCTURED. Rebranded from Global Citizen Year to Tilting Futures in 2024 and discontinued the original flagship 8-month Fellowship in favor of the shorter, lower-priced Take Action Lab. Students searching for 'Global Citizen Year' will find legacy marketing describing a program that no longer exists in that form, and legacy GCY URLs (go.globalcitizenyear.org) still resolve. The organization itself is enrolling for February and June 2027.

deadlines.note: Applications open for February 2027 and June 2027 cohorts; rolling review with priority rounds. Check the Dates & Deadlines section of the admissions page for exact rounds.

caveat_note: The user's suspicion was half right: Global Citizen Year did not close, but it did restructure significantly - new name, new program, much shorter duration. A family comparing against old $32,000-$36,000 GCY Fellowship figures is looking at a discontinued product. The current $21,000 semester is a different and shorter offering. 'No hidden costs' marketing coexists with a separate tuition-breakdown document and evidence that flights are a student expense; read the breakdown before signing.

name: Thinking Beyond Borders Gap Year
summary: DEFUNCT. TBB ran a two-semester, six-country gap year built around global development seminars, homestays and service work from 2008 until roughly 2020. It no longer operates.
other_eligibility: N/A - program no longer operating.
cost_note: DO NOT PAY THIS OPERATOR. No current price exists. Historically the full-year six-country program was priced in the mid-to-high $30,000s excluding airfare, but that number is obsolete and is noted only so families recognize stale marketing. Any current solicitation quoting a TBB price should be treated as suspect.
college_credit_note: Historically offered credit via a partner institution. Moot - program does not operate.
funding_note: CLOSED. EIN 26-0157032. The most recent Form 990 on file covers the fiscal year ending August 2017 (FY2016 revenue approximately $1.57 million), and the organization is NOT listed in the IRS's most recent list of tax-exempt organizations - GuideStar flags that it has not appeared on the IRS Business Master File for many months and may have merged or ceased operations. Its website (thinkingbeyondborders.org) returns HTTP 404 despite the domain still resolving, and social and directory activity stops around April 2020. The combination of lapsed tax-exempt status, no filings since 2017 and a dead website is conclusive in practice.
caveat_note: TBB is a textbook case of the problem this directory solves: the brand still has an active-looking Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and LinkedIn presence, GoOverseas and TeenLife listings, and high school counseling PDFs recommending it alongside Where There Be Dragons and Dynamy. All of that is stale. The domain still resolves in DNS but serves a 404, which makes casual verification misleading. Confidence is medium only because no formal dissolution notice was located; the IRS delisting plus seven years of non-filing is strong evidence.

name: LeapYear (formerly LEAPNOW)
operator: Naropa University (program absorbed from LEAPNOW: Transforming Education)
summary: RESTRUCTURED. LeapYear is a full-academic-year gap program combining international travel in Latin America or India with inner-development work and rites of passage, carrying 29 accredited college credits. The independent operator LEAPNOW no longer runs it standalone - leapnow.org now redirects to Naropa University.
other_eligibility: Application and interview; the program has a strong contemplative and personal-development orientation that is not a fit for everyone. Naropa is a Buddhist-inspired university.
cost_note: PRICE NOT CONFIRMED. No current published LeapYear tuition figure could be verified: the former LEAPNOW pricing pages are gone and Naropa's own program page did not surface a LeapYear-specific number. For scale only, Naropa's general undergraduate tuition and fees are estimated at about $38,758 for 2026 at $1,175 per credit hour, and LeapYear carries 29 credits - but do NOT treat that as the LeapYear price, which has historically been bundled differently. Tuition has historically included all scheduled program activities, food and accommodation during the program, the 29 credits, post-program internship placements and alumni reunions. Airfare treatment is not confirmed. Contact Naropa admissions (admissions@naropa.edu, 303-546-3595) for a written quote and an explicit statement of what is excluded.
financial_aid_note: Because the program is delivered through an accredited university, students reportedly have full access to federal and state financial aid via FAFSA plus private scholarships. This is a genuine structural advantage over non-accredited gap programs - but confirm current eligibility directly, since the delivery structure changed.
college_credit_note: 29 college credits for the year, granted by NAROPA UNIVERSITY (Boulder, Colorado), an accredited institution. CRITICAL WARNING: 29 credits is essentially a full year of college. A student completing LeapYear and then applying elsewhere will almost certainly be treated as a TRANSFER student, not an entering first-year student. Transfer status typically forfeits incoming-freshman merit scholarships, first-year-only institutional grants, guaranteed housing and honors-college eligibility, and it can void a deferred admission offer entirely. It also consumes federal aid eligibility - Pell and subsidized loan lifetime limits are drawn down by this year. If your plan is to matriculate at a different college as a freshman afterward, this program is structurally in tension with that plan. Get written confirmation from the destination college before enrolling.
funding_note: RESTRUCTURED, and the independent operator appears to be gone. leapnow.org now issues a 301 permanent redirect to naropa.edu, indicating LEAPNOW: Transforming Education (formerly of Calistoga, California) no longer operates the program as a standalone entity and the program has been folded into Naropa University. Naropa itself is a small private university; families should note that small-college financial fragility is a real sector-wide risk and should ask about program continuity guarantees. The Naropa page reached during research did not itself surface LeapYear content, so the program's current status and cadence should be verified by phone before applying.

deadlines.note: Historically a September start with rolling admissions. Verify current cycle directly with Naropa.

caveat_note: Price could not be confirmed and the program's current operating cadence under Naropa is unclear - the university's own site did not readily surface LeapYear program detail during research, which is itself a caution flag. Students will still find LEAPNOW-branded listings on GoOverseas, StudyAbroad101 and Verge Magazine describing an independent organization that no longer exists in that form. The 29-credit structure is the single most consequential fact here and is under-disclosed in legacy marketing.

name: Dynamy Internship Year
summary: Domestic US gap year in Worcester, Massachusetts built around three sequential internships plus supported independent apartment living, for students aged 17-22. One of the oldest US gap programs and unusual for being internship-based rather than travel-based.
other_eligibility: Interview and references. Students live semi-independently in apartments, so demonstrated readiness for independent living matters more than academics.
cost_note: 2026-2027 full Internship Year: tuition $27,650 PLUS housing $11,000 = $38,650 total. Single semester (Fall 2026 or Spring 2027): tuition $13,750 plus housing $6,500 = $20,250. NOTE the two-line pricing - the $27,650 headline is NOT the real number; housing is mandatory and adds $11,000. ADDITIONAL COSTS on top: a $400 refundable apartment damage deposit explicitly not included in the fees; optional stipend plan $25/semester; optional college courses through Clark University at $1,750 each or University of Montana at $1,950/semester. Meals are NOT included - students shop and cook for themselves, so budget realistically $2,500-$4,000/year for food. No airfare needed for most US students, which materially improves the comparison against overseas programs. All-in realistic cost for the full year is roughly $41,000-$43,000.
financial_aid_note: Need-based aid distributed FIRST-COME, FIRST-SERVED via the School and Student Service (SSS) for Financial Aid form - apply as early as possible, since late applicants can be shut out of a depleted pool regardless of need. 529 Savings Plans can be applied toward tuition when the student is enrolled in University of Montana courses, which is a meaningful tax advantage worth structuring for.
college_credit_note: Optional college courses are available at additional cost through CLARK UNIVERSITY ($1,750 per course) and UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA ($1,950 per semester); these are the credit-granting institutions, not Dynamy. WARNING: taking these credits converts an otherwise credit-free gap year into one that can trigger transfer-applicant classification at your destination college, forfeiting incoming-freshman merit scholarships and first-year-only institutional aid, and potentially invalidating a deferred admission. Because credit here is optional and priced separately, students who want to protect freshman status can simply decline it - a genuine advantage of this program's structure. Confirm with your college's registrar in writing either way.
funding_note: Enrollment open for Spring 2026 and the 2026-2027 Internship Year. Dynamy operates as a program of the Seven Hills Foundation, a large Massachusetts human-services nonprofit, which provides more institutional backing and counterparty stability than a standalone small operator.

deadlines.note: Rolling admissions. Financial aid is first-come first-served, so the effective deadline for aid is much earlier than the admission deadline.

caveat_note: The split tuition/housing presentation understates true cost by $11,000 for the year - always quote the $38,650 combined figure to families. Internships at Dynamy are UNPAID placements that the student pays roughly $38,650 to access; this is the clearest example in the directory of a program where the participant pays a premium for work experience that other pathways compensate. Compare directly against a paid AmeriCorps or apprenticeship year. The absence of airfare and the optional-credit structure are the two genuine advantages.

name: Kroka Expeditions Semester Programs (including tuition-free Full Circle Semester)
summary: Wilderness expedition semesters in New Hampshire, Vermont, the American Southeast and Ecuador for students aged 15-22, built around human-powered travel, farming and self-sufficiency. Notable for a donor-subsidized sliding-scale tuition model and one genuinely tuition-free semester.
other_eligibility: Physically demanding; health screen and fitness expectations. Age ranges vary by program: Roaring Canyons 15-18, Full Circle 16-21, Eastern Hellbender 18-22, Ecuador 18-21. Gap-year-age students should look at Eastern Hellbender and Ecuador.
cost_note: STANDOUT VALUE. The 2026 Full Circle Semester is TUITION-FREE - Kroka is covering tuition entirely through donor and foundation support. Families pay only fees, which Kroka guarantees will not exceed $4,000 per person (final figure announced to enrolled families by 1 January). ADDITIONAL: a $2,000 enrollment deposit is required, which functions as a contingency account for unexpected personal expenses during the semester and is REFUNDED to the family on successful completion - so it is a cash-flow requirement, not a true cost. Families must also buy, borrow or make items from the packing list (outdoor gear can run $500-$1,500 if starting from nothing - budget for it). Kroka states it CANNOT offer additional financial aid toward these fees, so the ~$4,000 is a hard floor for the tuition-free semester. Other Kroka semesters use full-cost tuition or donor-supported sliding-scale tuition based on household income; specific dollar amounts for those were not published and must be requested. No airfare needed for the domestic programs; the Ecuador semester will require international airfare, not confirmed as included.
financial_aid_note: Over half of Kroka families receive some form of financial aid. Two tuition pathways exist for standard semesters: full-cost tuition, and donor-supported sliding-scale tuition set by household income. Note the exception: the tuition-free Full Circle Semester carries NO additional aid for its ~$4,000 fee component.
college_credit_note: Kroka semesters are primarily high-school-level or experiential rather than college-credit-bearing; credit is not the core offering. This is arguably an advantage for gap students - no credit means no risk of being reclassified as a transfer applicant and no risk to incoming-freshman merit scholarships or first-year-only institutional aid. Confirm directly if you need credit.
funding_note: Active and enrolling through 2027. The tuition-free model depends on donor and foundation support, which by nature is year-to-year and not guaranteed to repeat - do not assume the tuition-free semester will exist in future cycles.

deadlines.note: Rolling by program; Fall 2026 Roaring Canyons is already full. Final fee figure for Full Circle announced to enrolled families by 1 January.

caveat_note: Kroka is the cheapest participant-pays option indexed here by a wide margin and deserves prominence for that reason. Two honest caveats: the $2,000 refundable deposit is real cash a family must front, and gear costs are genuinely not trivial for a family with no outdoor equipment. Tuition amounts for the non-tuition-free semesters are not published online, which limits comparison - request them in writing. Programs are physically demanding and are not a fit for every student.

name: HMI Gap
summary: Wilderness expedition gap semesters travelling through Colorado, Utah and Chilean Patagonia in groups of 8-12 students with 2-3 instructors, focused on backcountry skills, conservation and leadership. Fall runs about 80 days and spring about 60 days.
other_eligibility: Health and fitness screen; extended backcountry travel. Passport required for the Patagonia component.
cost_note: Spring 2027 HMI Gap semester tuition is $15,400, which HMI expresses as $256/day over 60 days - this figure is CONFIRMED. The fall gap semester runs about 80 days; at the same daily rate that implies roughly $20,500, but THAT FALL FIGURE IS DERIVED, NOT CONFIRMED - request it in writing. Do NOT confuse these with the separate HMI Semester for high schoolers, which is $40,550 for 2026-27; that is a different product. Tuition includes room, board and all domestic travel during the program. EXCLUDES all flights to the program start and from the program end, including INTERNATIONAL flights to Chile for the Patagonia section - budget $900-$1,600. Also excludes personal gear. A STUDENT ACCOUNT DEPOSIT is required: $1,200 for fall, $1,600 for spring, with unused funds returned. Realistic spring all-in is roughly $17,000-$18,000 including airfare, before the refundable deposit.
financial_aid_note: Strong: HMI states it seeks to MEET THE FULL DEMONSTRATED NEED of every student accepted into an HMI program. This is a materially better aid posture than almost any commercial gap operator and makes HMI worth applying to even for families who assume they cannot afford it. Apply for aid concurrently with admission.
college_credit_note: HMI Gap is an experiential wilderness program and is not structured as a credit-bearing college course; credit is not the core offering. This means it generally does NOT put incoming-freshman status at risk - an advantage over credit-bearing programs like Verto or LeapYear, since no post-high-school credits means no transfer-applicant reclassification and no forfeiture of first-year merit scholarships or first-year-only institutional aid. If any credit option is offered, confirm the grantor and the aid implications with your college's registrar in writing.
funding_note: Established nonprofit school with a long operating history and a parallel high school semester program. No distress signals found.

deadlines.note: Rolling admissions with limited cohort size (8-12 students), so effective deadlines are early.

caveat_note: Confidence is medium because only the spring figure ($15,400) is confirmed; the fall price is extrapolated from HMI's stated daily rate. Families frequently confuse HMI Gap with the much more expensive HMI Semester for high schoolers ($40,550) - these are different programs and the directory should keep them distinct. The full-demonstrated-need aid commitment is the most important fact here and should be surfaced prominently.

name: Alzar Gap
summary: Gap semester run by Alzar School in Idaho and Chilean Patagonia, combining whitewater kayaking, outdoor leadership, Spanish and cultural exchange. Substantially cheaper than the school's high school semester product.
other_eligibility: Health and fitness screen; whitewater and backcountry components. Passport required for Chile.
cost_note: $17,600 for the 2026 Alzar Gap program, covering tuition, room and board. ADDITIONAL REQUIRED: a $500 student expense account, plus a $2,000 deposit (this deposit IS applied toward tuition, so it is not an extra cost, but it is required cash up front). EXCLUDES airfare to the Coyhaique, Chile area - this is a remote Patagonian destination and flights are expensive, realistically $1,300-$2,200 from most US cities, often requiring a Santiago connection and a domestic Chilean leg. Realistic all-in is therefore about $19,400-$20,300, not $17,600. Do NOT confuse with Alzar's high school semester at $37,500 plus a $3,000 student account - a different and far more expensive product.
financial_aid_note: Need-based aid is offered and Alzar states many students receive it each semester; specific award sizes are not published. Request the aid decision before committing the $2,000 deposit.
college_credit_note: Alzar Gap is an experiential outdoor program rather than a credit-bearing academic term; credit is not the core offering. That is favorable for gap students - with no post-high-school credit there is no risk of being reclassified as a transfer applicant and no consequent forfeiture of incoming-freshman merit scholarships or first-year-only institutional aid. Confirm directly if credit matters to you.
funding_note: Operated by Alzar School, an established accredited semester school with its own campus in Idaho and a Chile base. The gap program is a secondary line alongside the core high school semester, which provides some institutional stability.

deadlines.note: Rolling admissions; small cohorts.

caveat_note: The airfare exclusion is unusually punishing here because Coyhaique is a genuinely remote destination - families who mentally budget $600 for 'a flight to South America' will be wrong by roughly $1,000. The $2,000 deposit applying to tuition is a fair structure and better than non-applicable deposits elsewhere. Verify the 2027 price, as the confirmed figure is for 2026.

name: Maximo Nivel Volunteer Abroad
summary: Low-cost, flexible volunteer, internship and Spanish-immersion placements in Antigua Guatemala, Cusco Peru, and San Jose and Manuel Antonio Costa Rica. Programs start every Monday year-round and run from 1 to 52 weeks.
other_eligibility: Generally open enrollment. Medical and healthcare placements may require relevant background or coursework.
cost_note: Published 2026 fees. Antigua Guatemala and Cusco Peru: 1 week $735, 2 weeks $995, 3 weeks $1,195, 4 weeks $1,395, each extra week $185. San Jose Costa Rica: 1 week $845, 2 weeks $1,145, 3 weeks $1,445, 4 weeks $1,715, extra week $195. Manuel Antonio Costa Rica: 2 weeks $1,245, 3 weeks $1,545, 4 weeks $1,815, extra week $195. SURCHARGE: an extra $95 PER WEEK applies to medical, conservation, eco-agriculture and construction projects - this is easy to miss and adds $380 to a four-week medical placement. Maximo Nivel states there is NO registration or processing fee, which is unusual and favorable in this sector. Fees include host-family accommodation (shared or private room) with breakfast and dinner seven days a week, airport transfers, activities and wifi. EXCLUDES international airfare (budget $500-$900 to Central America, $700-$1,200 to Peru), travel insurance, visa fees where applicable, lunches, and personal spending. A 12-week placement in Guatemala at $1,395 plus 8 extra weeks at $185 is $2,875 in fees, realistically $3,700-$4,000 all-in with flights and insurance.
financial_aid_note: No formal scholarship program identified. The low base price is the affordability mechanism here rather than aid.
college_credit_note: Maximo Nivel offers academic credit for Spanish coursework through university partners on request, and runs a separate study-abroad line. If you elect credit, note that post-high-school credit can cause a destination college to classify you as a transfer applicant, forfeiting incoming-freshman merit scholarships and first-year-only institutional aid, and potentially voiding a deferred admission. Volunteer-only placements without credit avoid this entirely. Confirm with your registrar in writing.
funding_note: Long-established, locally operated for-profit institute with its own physical campuses in each city rather than a booking-agent model. Actively publishing 2026 pricing.

deadlines.note: Programs begin every Monday year-round; effectively no deadline.

caveat_note: One of the cheapest structured options indexed - roughly $180-$200 per week at longer durations, versus $1,500-$2,000 per week for guided gap semesters. The tradeoff is far less structure, supervision and curriculum. The $95/week project surcharge on medical and conservation placements is the main hidden cost. As with all pay-to-volunteer models, students should think critically about whether unskilled short-term volunteer labor is genuinely useful to the host community, particularly for placements involving children or medical settings, where short-rotation foreign volunteers raise real safeguarding concerns.

name: Love Volunteers
summary: Low-cost volunteer placement organization connecting participants directly to local host projects in dozens of countries, deliberately positioned as a budget alternative to full-service gap providers. Fees are split between a registration fee paid to Love Volunteers and a program fee that largely goes to the local host.
other_eligibility: Varies by placement; some projects require background checks or relevant experience. Minimum age is typically 18 but some projects accept 17 with guardian consent.
cost_note: TWO-PART FEE STRUCTURE - both parts are mandatory. (1) REGISTRATION FEE of $299 for new volunteers ($149 for returning volunteers), paid to Love Volunteers, NON-REFUNDABLE once a placement is confirmed. (2) PROGRAM FEE paid separately and varying widely by destination - example structures include $582 for the first week plus $187 for each subsequent week on self-catered placements, and from $990 for two weeks on other placements such as Cameroon. So a four-week placement is realistically $299 + roughly $1,140 = about $1,440 in fees. Program fees typically cover airport pickup, orientation, accommodation, food, local transport and in-country support staff. EXCLUDES international airfare, travel insurance (normally mandatory), visa costs, vaccinations and personal spending - budget $1,000-$2,000 on top for a mid-length placement. Registration fees, while non-refundable, remain valid indefinitely and are transferable to another program or to a friend or family member, which is a genuinely fair term.
financial_aid_note: No scholarship program. Group and family discounts are available. Affordability comes from the low base price.
college_credit_note: No college credit is offered. For a gap student this is an advantage in one specific respect: with no post-high-school credits earned, there is no risk of being reclassified as a transfer applicant and no consequent forfeiture of incoming-freshman merit scholarships or first-year-only institutional aid.
funding_note: Actively operating and taking bookings. Small organization operating a referral/placement model rather than running programs directly, which means less institutional depth than a program operator if something goes wrong in country.

deadlines.note: Rolling; placements arranged continuously.

caveat_note: Love Volunteers is a PLACEMENT AGENT, not a program operator - it brokers a connection to a local host project and the local host delivers the experience. Supervision, safeguarding practice and quality therefore vary substantially by individual project rather than being guaranteed by the brand. Students placed in orphanages, children's homes or medical settings should scrutinize the safeguarding arrangements carefully; short-rotation foreign volunteering with vulnerable children is widely criticized by child-protection organizations. Exact per-destination pricing is not centrally published, so verify the specific number for your placement in writing before paying the non-refundable $299.

name: African Impact Volunteer Projects
summary: Structured volunteer and internship placements across South Africa, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Zambia, Kenya, Mozambique, Malawi, Madagascar and the Seychelles, spanning wildlife conservation, teaching, community development and healthcare. Runs its own in-country bases rather than brokering placements.
other_eligibility: Minimum age typically 18 (some projects 17 with consent). Healthcare and medical placements require relevant study or qualifications. Background checks apply to projects involving children.
cost_note: Advertised 'from $1,950' for the Zambia teaching and community development project; per-duration pricing (2, 4, 8, 12 weeks) is NOT published on the project pages and must be requested, so the upper bound is unconfirmed. Project fees include accommodation, meals, project equipment and resources, arrival and departure transfers, 24/7 support and in-country orientation. EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED per African Impact: visa costs, travel insurance, private transfers, optional weekend activities, snacks and souvenirs. International airfare is also excluded and is substantial for southern and east Africa - realistically $1,100-$1,900 from the US. Visa costs for Zambia, Tanzania and Kenya typically run $50-$160. A four-week placement advertised at $1,950 is therefore realistically $3,300-$4,200 all-in. Low-season rates were offered for arrivals 1 December 2025 to 25 May 2026. Deposit amount not published.
financial_aid_note: No scholarship program identified. Fundraising toolkits are provided rather than aid.
college_credit_note: Internships of four weeks minimum are offered and some universities will grant credit for them via the student's own institution, but African Impact is not itself a credit-granting body. If your home institution awards credit, be aware that post-high-school credit can trigger transfer-applicant classification at a destination college, forfeiting incoming-freshman merit scholarships and first-year-only institutional aid. Confirm with the registrar in writing.
funding_note: Established operator running its own bases in multiple countries, actively publishing 2026 seasonal rates. Operates alongside an affiliated charitable foundation.

deadlines.note: Rolling start dates; low-season pricing window ran 1 Dec 2025 to 25 May 2026.

caveat_note: Pricing is deliberately gated behind an enquiry form - only 'from' prices appear publicly, which makes honest comparison difficult and is a mild transparency concern. African Impact does disclose its exclusions clearly, which is better than average. As with all paid volunteering, examine whether the placement genuinely requires foreign volunteers; African Impact has moved away from orphanage volunteering, which is a positive safeguarding signal, but any project involving direct contact with children warrants scrutiny of vetting and rotation practices.

name: Plan My Gap Year (PMGY)
summary: UK-based budget volunteer placement organization offering programs from 1 to 40 weeks across 17 destinations in Africa, Asia, Europe and South America, priced on a per-day basis. Among the lowest-cost structured options available.
other_eligibility: Typically 18+ (some destinations accept 17 with consent). Travel insurance is MANDATORY for all volunteers. Some placements require background checks.
cost_note: PRICED PER DAY, which makes headline comparison misleading - the cents figures above are the DAILY rate, not a program total. Published from-rates: Sri Lanka from $24/day, Ghana from $26/day, Peru from $27/day. A four-week placement in Ghana is therefore roughly $728; twelve weeks roughly $2,184. Daily fee includes accommodation, meals, airport pickup, in-country orientation, pre-departure support and 24-hour hosted support. EXCLUDED: international flights (budget $900-$1,600 depending on destination); TRAVEL INSURANCE, which PMGY makes MANDATORY and sells through a partner insurer (budget $60-$250 depending on duration); visa fees; vaccinations; and personal spending. A REGISTRATION FEE is charged to secure a place, with the balance of the program fee due 60 days before start - the registration fee amount is not published on the homepage and must be confirmed before applying. A 12-week Ghana placement at roughly $2,184 is realistically $3,400-$4,200 all-in.
financial_aid_note: No scholarship program. Fundraising guidance is provided instead. The low daily rate is the affordability mechanism.
college_credit_note: No college credit is offered. For a gap student this is structurally protective: no post-high-school credits means no risk of transfer-applicant reclassification and no forfeiture of incoming-freshman merit scholarships or first-year-only institutional aid.
funding_note: Actively operating with 2026 and 2027 programs. Note the domain migrated from planmygapyear.co.uk to planmygapyear.com; the old domain 301-redirects, so both are legitimate. Small UK operator - less institutional depth than large providers.

deadlines.note: Monthly start dates across destinations. Balance of program fee due 60 days before start.

caveat_note: The per-day pricing model makes PMGY look far cheaper than it is in a directory that lists other programs as totals - always convert to a program total before comparing. The registration fee is referenced but not quantified publicly, which is a transparency gap; get it in writing. Mandatory insurance sold through a partner is a modest conflict of interest worth noting, though the requirement itself is reasonable. Standard paid-volunteering caveats apply: scrutinize placements involving children, and be realistic about what unskilled short-term volunteers contribute.

name: Operation Wallacea Research Expeditions
summary: Biodiversity research expeditions in Honduras, Mexico, Indonesia, Fiji, Peru, South Africa and elsewhere, where participants collect data alongside academic scientists on genuine long-term monitoring projects. Structured mainly around school groups and university dissertation students rather than individual gap-year enrollment.
other_eligibility: School-group expeditions require enrollment through a participating school. Dissertation and research-assistant placements generally require current university enrollment in a relevant field. Dive-based expeditions require medical clearance and often prior certification.
cost_note: PRICE NOT CONFIRMED - Operation Wallacea does not publish expedition prices publicly. Opwall states there is a standard fee paid to it for all expeditions, but the total varies with departure airport, group size and payment method, and quotes are issued directly to group leaders rather than posted online. TWO BOOKING MODELS: a package including international flights, internal travel and expedition costs; or an expedition-elements-only booking where you arrange your own travel. Because of this, a family cannot compare Opwall against a priced program without first requesting a quote. Historically expeditions have run in the low-to-mid thousands for one to two weeks, but no current figure could be verified and NO PRICE SHOULD BE ASSUMED. Request a written quote specifying whether flights, insurance, visas and dive certification are inside or outside the number.
financial_aid_note: Opwall publicizes fundraising support and some bursary routes via schools rather than direct scholarships. Not confirmed for individual gap-year applicants.
college_credit_note: Opwall supports university dissertation fieldwork, and credit where it exists is granted by the student's OWN home university, not by Opwall. For a post-high-school gap student this typically means no credit is earned and therefore no risk to incoming-freshman status. If your institution does award credit, confirm with its registrar whether it affects entering-student classification, since that can forfeit incoming-freshman merit scholarships and first-year-only institutional aid.
funding_note: Actively publishing school expedition dates. Long-running organization with genuine peer-reviewed scientific output, which distinguishes it from voluntourism operators.

deadlines.note: Expeditions run in a summer field season; group bookings are arranged many months ahead through school leaders.

caveat_note: Confidence is low purely because no price is publicly available - the science and operating status are well established. The structural caveat for this directory's audience is that Opwall is not really an individual gap-year product: it is oriented to school groups and university dissertation students, so a solo post-high-school student may find limited entry routes. The research contribution is genuine, which is a meaningful contrast with pay-to-volunteer programs, but the participant still pays and receives no compensation.

name: Frontier Volunteer and Gap Year Projects
operator: The Society for Environmental Exploration (trading as Frontier)
summary: DEFUNCT. Frontier sold conservation, teaching and adventure volunteer placements to UK and international gap-year students from 1989, advertising 400+ projects worldwide. Its parent company was formally dissolved in September 2023.
other_eligibility: N/A - organization dissolved.
cost_note: DO NOT PAY THIS OPERATOR. No current price exists; the company is dissolved. For historical recognition only, participants reported paying around $13,000 for a 30-week placement plus roughly $1,700 extra for dive certifications, with flights, insurance and visas all additional on top. Any site currently quoting a Frontier price and accepting a deposit should be treated as fraudulent or as a stale listing.
college_credit_note: Historically advertised BTEC-style certifications and dive qualifications rather than US college credit. Moot - organization dissolved.
funding_note: CLOSED AND FORMALLY DISSOLVED. The Society for Environmental Exploration, UK company number 02374609, registered at 50-52 Rivington Street, London EC2A 3QP, was DISSOLVED ON 26 SEPTEMBER 2023 per the UK Companies House register. Consistent with this, the frontier.ac.uk domain no longer resolves in DNS at all - both frontier.ac.uk and www.frontier.ac.uk return NXDOMAIN as of August 2026, meaning the domain registration has lapsed entirely.
caveat_note: This is the clearest closure case in the set and the verification is authoritative (Companies House dissolution plus a dead domain). Despite that, Frontier remains listed as bookable on third-party marketplaces including Volunteer World, Volunteer Forever, GoOverseas and K12Academics, and search engines still surface cached frontier.ac.uk pages that look live. Students WILL find these and may attempt to book. Even before dissolution, Frontier drew sustained public criticism over pricing transparency and value for money, with volunteers questioning how much of the fee reached the projects. Flag prominently as gone.

name: YWAM Discipleship Training School (DTS)
operator: Youth With A Mission (independent local bases)
summary: Five-to-six-month Christian missions training program run independently by hundreds of local YWAM bases worldwide, structured as a classroom lecture phase followed by an overseas outreach phase. Prices, quality and oversight vary substantially between bases because each operates autonomously.
other_eligibility: EXPLICIT FAITH REQUIREMENT - DTS is a Christian discipleship program and applicants are expected to be practicing Christians; the curriculum is devotional and evangelistic. Application includes pastoral references. Minimum age is typically 18, with separate youth versions at some bases.
cost_note: TWO SEPARATE MANDATORY FEES that families routinely under-budget, because bases advertise the lecture-phase price prominently and the outreach price separately. LECTURE PHASE (US bases, 2026): YWAM Ships Kona $4,700; YWAM Raleigh NC $4,695; YWAM Los Angeles $4,000; YWAM Madison $3,995 plus conference fees; YWAM Tyler $3,960; YWAM Wylie $3,850. This covers room, board and tuition but NOT airfare to the base. OUTREACH PHASE, billed separately and driven mostly by airfare to the field assignment: YWAM Wylie $5,000-$6,000; YWAM Ships Kona $5,000-$5,500; YWAM Madison $3,000-$4,500; YWAM Raleigh NC $2,485 PLUS airfare. TOTAL realistic range is therefore roughly $6,300-$10,200 depending on base and outreach destination, plus your own travel to the base at the start, passport, visas and vaccinations. Many students do not learn the outreach figure until partway through the lecture phase, by which point they are committed. ASK FOR THE OUTREACH ESTIMATE IN WRITING BEFORE ENROLLING.
financial_aid_note: There is no institutional financial aid. The expected funding model is personal SUPPORT-RAISING - students write to churches, family and friends soliciting donations to cover fees. This works well for students embedded in a supportive congregation and poorly for those who are not, and it is a materially different proposition from need-based aid. Some bases offer limited work-scholarship arrangements.
college_credit_note: DTS is generally NOT accredited for US college credit, though a small number of bases have arrangements with Christian colleges or the University of the Nations (YWAM's own unaccredited-in-the-US institution) to recognize the coursework. Do not assume transferability. The upside for gap students is that with no transferable post-high-school credit there is normally no risk of transfer-applicant reclassification and no forfeiture of incoming-freshman merit scholarships or first-year-only institutional aid. If a base claims credit, verify with your destination college's registrar in writing before relying on it.
funding_note: YWAM as a movement is large and active, but there is NO central financial guarantee: each base is a separate legal and financial entity. The strength of the international brand does not transfer to the solvency, insurance or safeguarding practice of the individual base you enroll with. Vet the specific base, not YWAM generally.

deadlines.note: Each base sets its own start dates, typically with spring and fall intakes. Deadlines vary by base.

caveat_note: PARTICIPANT PAYS, despite this being a missions program that outsiders sometimes assume is funded - and the true cost is roughly double the advertised lecture-phase price once outreach is included. The decentralized structure is the central risk: staff qualifications, background-check practice, child-protection policy, medical support and insurance vary enormously between bases, and YWAM has faced public safeguarding criticism at particular locations over the years. Families should ask a specific base directly for its child-protection policy, staff vetting procedure, insurance arrangements and a written total-cost estimate including outreach. The support-raising funding model can also place real social pressure on an 18-year-old to solicit money from their community.

name: Catholic Volunteer Network Member Programs (JVC, JVC Northwest, Christian Appalachian Project, Red Cloud and 150+ others)
operator: Catholic Volunteer Network (directory of independent member programs)
summary: PAYS RATHER THAN CHARGES. Catholic Volunteer Network is a directory of 150+ independent faith-based full-time service programs, the large majority of which provide housing, food and a modest monthly living stipend rather than charging a participation fee. Placements are typically one year in US communities, with some international options.
other_eligibility: VARIES BY MEMBER PROGRAM AND THIS MATTERS. Many of the best-known members - notably Jesuit Volunteer Corps and JVC Northwest - REQUIRE A BACHELOR'S DEGREE and are post-undergraduate only, so they are not open to a post-high-school gap student. Others accept 18+ without a degree. Faith requirements also vary: some require active Catholic practice, many welcome volunteers of any faith or none while retaining a Catholic identity and communal spiritual practice. Filter carefully by degree requirement and faith expectation before applying.
pay_note: Most member programs provide a modest monthly living stipend for personal expenses on top of full room and board - commonly in the range of roughly $100-$500 per month depending on the program and location, though individual programs vary and some fall outside this band. The stipend is explicitly designed for simple living, not as a wage, and will not build savings. The substantive economic value is in the housing and food, not the cash. Many programs additionally arrange student loan DEFERMENT for the service year, and some offer education awards or loan-repayment assistance on completion.
cost_note: NO PROGRAM FEE at the great majority of member programs - this is the key distinction from every commercial operator in this directory. Programs provide basic room and board plus a monthly stipend, and CVN states most volunteers live within their stipend and incur no debt during service. Genuine out-of-pocket items are limited and typically include a pre-service medical exam, passport and visa where the placement is international, personal travel to orientation in some cases, and personal spending beyond the stipend. A minority of member programs - particularly international ones - do ask volunteers to raise a fundraising contribution; check each program individually rather than assuming. Because room, board and a stipend are provided, this is a genuinely different money direction from a $17,950 pay-to-participate semester.
financial_aid_note: Not applicable in the usual sense since there is no fee. Instead look for the reverse: loan deferment during service, education awards on completion, and in some programs AmeriCorps affiliation that carries a Segal Education Award. Ask each program whether it is AmeriCorps-affiliated, as that materially changes the financial picture.
college_credit_note: Service years generally do not carry college credit, and some member programs instead offer graduate-school tuition partnerships or discounts for alumni. The absence of credit is protective for a gap student: no post-high-school credit means no risk of being reclassified as a transfer applicant and no forfeiture of incoming-freshman merit scholarships or first-year-only institutional aid.
funding_note: CVN itself is a network and directory, not the program operator - it does not place volunteers or hold their money. Financial health must be assessed at the individual member program level. Faith-based service programs have contracted somewhat over the past decade as religious affiliation has declined, so confirm any specific program is still running its current cycle rather than relying on the directory listing.

deadlines.note: Most member programs run an August start with applications opening in the fall and priority deadlines between January and March. Deadlines are set by each member program, not by CVN.

caveat_note: IMPORTANT DIRECTORY NOTE: do not treat this as one program. It is an index of 150+ independent programs with widely varying eligibility, stipends, faith expectations and quality. The two facts that most change a student's shortlist are (1) many flagship members require a completed bachelor's degree and are closed to post-high-school students, and (2) the money direction is PAY, not charge - a student choosing between this and a $17,950 gap semester is facing roughly a $20,000-$25,000 swing in either direction. Confidence is medium because the stipend range is a sector generalization rather than a single verified figure; verify the exact stipend with the specific program.

name: Young Adults in Global Mission (YAGM)
summary: PAYS RATHER THAN CHARGES. A year-long international accompaniment program placing young adults with Lutheran partner churches and organizations in country programs worldwide, providing round-trip airfare, full room and board, health insurance and a monthly stipend. Participants are asked to help fundraise but are not charged tuition.
other_eligibility: Typically ages 21-29, so this is generally a POST-UNDERGRADUATE option and NOT open to a student straight out of high school - an important filter. Rooted in the Lutheran tradition; applicants of other Christian backgrounds are often welcomed but the program is explicitly faith-based and involves accompaniment with partner churches. Medical and psychological clearance required.
pay_note: Volunteers receive a modest monthly stipend explicitly calibrated so they can live at an economic level similar to that of their host community - the ELCA describes it as neither a salary nor an hourly wage, and the exact amount varies by country program and is not published. On top of the stipend, YAGM provides ROUND-TRIP INTERNATIONAL AIRFARE to and from the country of service, full room and board, all US-based training events, transportation to in-country retreats, basic international travelers' health insurance and a mental health support program. The ELCA states it costs the church approximately $15,000 to support one volunteer for a year - that is the church's cost, NOT a bill to the participant.
cost_note: NO TUITION OR PROGRAM FEE. The only meaningful participant-side financial obligation is a FUNDRAISING EXPECTATION: participants are invited to fundraise alongside supporters, and some sponsoring congregations require each participant to raise about $4,000. This is a real obligation and should be planned for, but it is fundamentally different from a fee - it is raised from a community rather than paid from family savings, it is typically supported by the sponsoring congregation's own network, and failure to hit the full target does not generally bar participation in the way an unpaid tuition bill would. Airfare, insurance, housing and food are all COVERED, which is the reverse of every commercial operator in this directory. Genuine out-of-pocket items: passport, some vaccinations, personal spending beyond the stipend, and travel to US training events if not covered. Net position for most participants is roughly break-even to modestly positive.
financial_aid_note: Not applicable - there is no fee to offset. The relevant support mechanism is congregational and personal fundraising, for which the ELCA provides infrastructure and a donation portal. Ask whether your sponsoring congregation sets a hard fundraising floor.
college_credit_note: No college credit is offered; this is a service and accompaniment year, not an academic program. For anyone holding a deferred admission this is protective - with no post-high-school credit earned there is no risk of transfer-applicant reclassification and no forfeiture of incoming-freshman merit scholarships or first-year-only institutional aid. In practice the 21+ age floor means most participants have already completed a degree.
funding_note: Active with applications open on a rolling basis for the 2027-2028 and 2028-2029 service years. Funded through ELCA denominational giving, which has been under long-term pressure as US mainline membership declines - country programs have been added and retired over the years, so confirm your target country program is still running. The program itself shows no sign of ending.

deadlines.note: Priority deadline 15 January. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis before this.
Final deadline 1 February.

caveat_note: Flagged in response to the brief's specific question: YAGM PAYS, it does not charge. The $15,000 figure that appears in ELCA materials is the church's cost to support a volunteer and is frequently misread by students as a price tag - it is not. The genuine constraints are the age floor of about 21 (which excludes most post-high-school gap students), the faith-based framing, the competitive selection, and the roughly $4,000 fundraising expectation at some congregations. Placement countries are assigned by the program rather than chosen by the applicant.

name: Serving And Learning Together (SALT)
summary: PAYS RATHER THAN CHARGES. An 11-month international service assignment running August to July for US and Canadian young adults, with MCC covering travel, housing, food, in-country transport and full medical coverage plus a monthly stipend. There is no program fee.
other_eligibility: OPEN TO CANADIAN AND US CITIZENS ONLY - citizenship is a hard gate. Faith-based: MCC is an Anabaptist/Mennonite agency and applicants are expected to be committed Christians willing to engage with local church communities, though applicants are not required to be Mennonite. Selection emphasizes communication skills, cultural openness and flexibility. Assignments are matched by MCC rather than chosen freely.
pay_note: Participants receive a monthly stipend for personal items such as clothing, vacations and haircuts; MCC does not publish the exact amount, so request it. Beyond the stipend, MCC provides ALL basic needs related to the assignment: travel to and from the assignment, food and household costs, housing, in-country transportation, orientation and re-entry travel, vacation days, and FULL MEDICAL COVERAGE WITH NO CO-PAYS. MCC also provides STUDENT LOAN REPAYMENT ASSISTANCE during service and for three months afterward, which is an unusually valuable benefit for a recent graduate and can be worth thousands of dollars.
cost_note: NO PROGRAM FEE - MCC states this explicitly. Participant out-of-pocket costs are limited to: a REQUIRED pre-service medical exam, optional optical and dental exams, passport and visa expenses, and any vaccinations relevant to the placement country. Realistically that is a few hundred dollars, largely recoverable if the participant has health insurance. SEPARATELY, each SALT participant is expected to raise a minimum financial CONTRIBUTION equivalent to roughly half of MCC's average per-participant cost - MCC does not publish the dollar figure, so ask for it directly and in writing, as it is the single number that determines whether this is truly cost-free for you. This is a fundraising target raised from a supporting community, not a tuition bill, and it sits alongside covered airfare, housing, food, insurance and a stipend. Net position for most participants is break-even to positive, and the loan-repayment assistance can make it clearly positive.
financial_aid_note: Not applicable - there is no fee. The relevant financial features are the covered costs, the monthly stipend, and the student loan repayment assistance during service and for three months after. MCC provides fundraising support for the required contribution.
college_credit_note: No college credit is offered. For a student holding deferred admission this is protective - no post-high-school credit means no risk of being reclassified as a transfer applicant, and therefore no forfeiture of incoming-freshman merit scholarships or first-year-only institutional aid.
funding_note: Active and recruiting. MCC is a large, long-established and financially solid international relief and development agency with broad denominational and donor support. Counterparty risk is low.

deadlines.note: Only applications received before 15 February are guaranteed consideration for placement in the same year. Assignment runs August to July.

caveat_note: Flagged in response to the brief's specific question: SALT PAYS, it does not charge. The one thing that could change that conclusion is the required minimum financial contribution, whose dollar amount MCC does not publish - it is described only as roughly half of MCC's average per-participant cost, which for comparable programs implies something in the low-to-mid four figures. Get that number in writing before treating SALT as free. The citizenship gate (US/Canada only) and the Christian faith expectation are firm eligibility limits. Note also that SALT is one year and assignments are matched by MCC, so applicants with a fixed geographic preference may be disappointed.

name: Birthright Israel Onward
operator: Birthright Israel Onward / regional Jewish federations and Hillels
summary: Heavily subsidized 6-8 week summer internship and fellowship program in Israeli cities, placing participants in professional internships alongside housing, educational programming and travel. Priced far below market because of philanthropic and federation subsidy.
other_eligibility: Open to Jewish young adults, typically ages 18-27, usually current university students or recent graduates. Eligibility, pricing and application run through a sponsoring community - a regional federation, Hillel or partner organization - and terms vary by that sponsor. Many participants combine it with a free 10-day Birthright trip to obtain subsidized airfare.
cost_note: $999 program fee for the summer 2026 cycle (dates 4 June - 29 July 2026), though the exact figure varies slightly by city because housing costs differ. The fee covers housing, educational programming, program staff, basic medical insurance and ground transportation - remarkable value for eight weeks and a function of heavy philanthropic subsidy. EXCLUDED and material: FLIGHTS (budget $900-$1,600 round trip to Tel Aviv from the US), FOOD for the full eight weeks (budget $600-$1,200), and phone service. DEPOSIT: a $400 credit card authorization is required as a participation and security deposit - this is a hold rather than an automatic charge, but families need available credit for it. Realistic all-in is therefore roughly $2,500-$3,800, still far below any commercial equivalent. TIP: participants who append Onward to a free 10-day Birthright trip can use Birthright's included flight (airline extension fees apply), which can remove most of the airfare cost - this is the single biggest available saving.
financial_aid_note: The $999 price already reflects deep subsidy. Additional need-based grants are frequently available through the sponsoring federation or Hillel - ask the local sponsor directly, as these are not advertised centrally.
college_credit_note: Onward is an internship and immersion program and generally does not carry college credit, though some sponsoring universities arrange internship credit through the student's own institution. Where credit is granted by your home institution, confirm with its registrar whether it affects entering-student classification - post-high-school credit can convert a deferred admit into a transfer applicant, forfeiting incoming-freshman merit scholarships and first-year-only institutional aid.
funding_note: Active with published summer 2026 dates and a broad network of federation and Hillel sponsors. Funding depends on philanthropic and Birthright-affiliated support, which is well established but is discretionary rather than contractual. Programming in Israel is also subject to suspension during periods of regional conflict - confirm current operating status and the sponsor's cancellation and refund policy before booking flights.

deadlines.note: Applications typically open in the fall for the following summer and are administered by the sponsoring federation or Hillel, each with its own deadline. Apply through your local sponsor, not centrally.

caveat_note: Best cost-per-week ratio of any participant-pays program indexed here - roughly $125/week in program fees for a professional internship with housing. Two honest caveats: eligibility is restricted to Jewish young adults, which makes it inapplicable to most of this directory's audience; and the region is subject to conflict-driven program suspension, so refund and cancellation terms matter more than usual, especially given that participants buy their own non-refundable flights. Confirm the sponsor's policy on what happens to your flight cost if the program is cancelled.

name: Middlebury Language Schools Summer Immersion
