summary: Seven-to-nine-week total-immersion summer language programs in Vermont, governed by a strict Language Pledge under which participants speak only the target language. Academically rigorous and credit-bearing, delivered by an accredited US college rather than a travel operator.
other_eligibility: Open to high school graduates, undergraduates, graduate students and adults; placement is by language proficiency assessment rather than age. Participants must sign and abide by the Language Pledge, which is enforced and can result in dismissal. Graduate-level programs require a bachelor's degree.
cost_note: Undergraduate/immersion summer sessions run approximately $6,750-$8,250 comprehensive, and that figure INCLUDES tuition, room AND board - unusually complete for this price band. Graduate-level programs are billed differently and cost more: the Spanish graduate program bills tuition $8,235 plus insurance $140 plus housing and food $3,990, totaling about $12,365. EXCLUDED across programs: transportation to and from Vermont (budget $200-$700 for domestic US travel), books and supplies, personal expenses, and health insurance where not itemized. Some language schools charge additional fees for materials, excursions and cultural activities - check the specific language's fee page, since costs differ by language. There is no international airfare requirement for the Vermont campuses, which materially improves the all-in comparison against overseas programs. Deposit amount varies by program; confirm at admission.
financial_aid_note: Middlebury offers need-based financial aid for the Language Schools, plus a range of fellowships and scholarships including support tied to specific languages and to teachers. Aid is meaningful and worth applying for; apply at the same time as admission, since funds are limited.
college_credit_note: Credit is granted by MIDDLEBURY COLLEGE, an accredited US institution, and Middlebury Language Schools credit is well regarded and widely transferable. WARNING, and it is a real one here precisely because the credit is legitimate: a summer session can yield a full year's worth of language credit. For a student holding a deferred college admission, post-high-school credit can cause the admitting college to reclassify them as a TRANSFER applicant rather than an entering first-year student, which typically forfeits incoming-freshman merit scholarships, first-year-only institutional grants and honors eligibility, and can invalidate the deferral. Confirm with your admitting college's registrar and financial aid office IN WRITING before enrolling. Students already enrolled in a college should confirm transferability with their own registrar.
funding_note: Operated by Middlebury College, a well-endowed accredited liberal arts institution. Counterparty risk is negligible relative to independent gap operators.

deadlines.note: Applications typically open in the fall with rolling review; popular languages fill early and financial aid consideration favors early applicants.

caveat_note: This is an academic program rather than a gap-year program, and it belongs in the directory mainly as a high-quality summer comparison point - it will not fill a full gap year. The credit-versus-freshman-aid interaction is the most consequential warning and is under-appreciated by students who think of a summer language course as harmless. Confidence is medium because per-language fees vary and the figures cited combine undergraduate immersion and graduate program pricing; verify the exact number on your specific language's dates-and-fees page.

name: CIEE Gap Year Abroad
summary: Semester-length language, internship and multi-destination gap programs in Seville, Paris, Kyoto, Shanghai, Florence, Seoul and multi-city European itineraries, run by a large established nonprofit study-abroad organization. Language programs are homestay-based with roughly 20 hours a week of instruction.
other_eligibility: High school graduate or equivalent. Student visa required for most destinations and is the participant's responsibility - Spain, Japan and China visas require lead time and documentation.
cost_note: $12,100 confirmed for the Seville Spanish Language & Culture semester, 21 January to 16 May 2026 (about 17 weeks). Other destinations are priced separately and CIEE does not publish them on the program-search page - request each directly. Fee includes tuition, homestay accommodation, medical and accident insurance, iNext travel insurance, on-site staff support, pre-departure advising and 24/7 emergency support. EXCLUDED: round-trip AIRFARE, which CIEE itself estimates at $600-$1,500; VISA costs; and spending money. Realistic all-in for Seville is therefore roughly $12,900-$14,000. DISCOUNT: a $400 priority-deadline discount applies for applications by 1 May for fall starts and 1 September for spring starts. Deposit amount not published; confirm before applying.
financial_aid_note: CIEE runs substantial scholarship and grant programs across its portfolio, including need-based awards and the CIEE Global Access Initiative; availability for the gap-year line specifically should be confirmed with an advisor. The $400 priority discount is effectively automatic if you apply early - do not miss it.
college_credit_note: The gap programs themselves are not primarily credit-bearing, but ALL CIEE Gap Year Abroad programs offer the option to take college-level coursework online at a discounted rate through ARIZONA STATE UNIVERSITY, which is the credit-granting institution. WARNING: electing that ASU coursework converts a credit-free gap semester into one that generates post-high-school college credit, which can cause a destination college to classify you as a TRANSFER applicant rather than an entering first-year student. That commonly forfeits incoming-freshman merit scholarships, first-year-only institutional grants and honors eligibility, and can invalidate a deferred admission offer. Because the credit is optional and separately priced, students who want to protect freshman status can simply decline it. Confirm with your admitting college's registrar in writing either way.
funding_note: CIEE is one of the largest and oldest US nonprofit international education organizations, with a broad portfolio well beyond gap programs. Counterparty risk is low.

deadlines.note: Priority deadline for fall starts; applying by this date secures a $400 discount.
Priority deadline for spring starts; $400 discount.

caveat_note: At about $12,100 for 17 weeks (roughly $710/week including homestay meals and 20 hours a week of instruction), CIEE is meaningfully better value than the guided-adventure operators in this category, and the institutional backing is stronger. The main frustration is that only some program prices are published - most require an enquiry, which impedes comparison. Confidence is medium because only the Seville figure was confirmed; do not extrapolate it to Kyoto, Shanghai or the multi-destination tours, which are likely higher.

name: AIFS Abroad Gap Year / Semester Abroad
operator: AIFS Abroad (American Institute For Foreign Study)
summary: Semester study and internship programs abroad with an all-inclusive fee structure that, unusually for this market, includes round-trip flights from US gateway cities. Primarily a university study-abroad provider with gap-year entry points.
other_eligibility: Most AIFS programs are designed for enrolled university students and may require a minimum GPA and completed college coursework; gap-year entry points exist but are narrower than the general study-abroad catalog. Confirm that a given program admits non-matriculated gap students before applying. Student visa required for most destinations.
cost_note: $19,790 quoted for Fall 2027 or Spring 2028 when applying by 1 September 2026 to lock prior-year pricing - this is one specific locked-rate offer, and AIFS prices vary substantially by destination and program, so treat $19,790 as indicative rather than universal. NOTABLY INCLUDED: round-trip FLIGHTS from 25 US gateway cities, housing, on-site staff, cultural activities and excursions, 24/7 emergency support, comprehensive insurance, academic credit, and carbon offsetting for flights. Because airfare is inside the fee, the effective comparison against a $17,000 program that excludes $1,500 of airfare is closer than the headline suggests. EXCLUDED: meals in many housing configurations, visa and passport fees, textbooks, and personal spending - budget $2,000-$4,000 for a semester of food if a meal plan is not included, plus $150-$500 for visas. Deposit required; amount not published.
financial_aid_note: AIFS offers scholarships and grants, and because programs are credit-bearing through host or partner universities, many enrolled students can apply existing federal and institutional financial aid via their home institution - a significant advantage over non-academic gap programs. Non-matriculated gap students generally CANNOT use home-institution aid, so verify your own status carefully.
college_credit_note: Academic credit is included and is granted through the host university abroad or an AIFS partner institution, then transcripted for transfer. WARNING, and it is significant here because the credit is a core feature rather than an add-on: a full semester of transferable credit earned after high school graduation can cause a college to classify you as a TRANSFER applicant instead of an entering first-year student, which typically forfeits incoming-freshman merit scholarships, first-year-only institutional grants, guaranteed housing and honors eligibility, and can convert a deferred admission into a fresh transfer application with no guarantee of readmission. It also draws down federal aid lifetime eligibility. If you hold a deferred admit, get the treatment confirmed in writing by that college's registrar and financial aid office BEFORE enrolling.
funding_note: AIFS is a long-established study-abroad provider operating since 1964 with its own global education centers. Counterparty risk is low.

deadlines.note: Apply by 1 September 2026 to lock prior-year pricing at the quoted $19,790 rate.

caveat_note: Included airfare is a genuine and rare advantage that makes AIFS more competitive than the headline price suggests - flag it. Two cautions: the $19,790 figure is one locked-rate promotional quote rather than a general price list, so verify for your destination; and AIFS is fundamentally a university study-abroad provider, so a post-high-school gap student must confirm they are actually eligible for the specific program rather than assuming the general catalog is open to them. The credit-versus-freshman-status interaction is the most consequential risk in this listing.
